steps.body: Count sides by running a finger along each straight edge: one, turn at the corner, two, turn — until you arrive back home.
steps.narration: Count sides by running a finger along each straight edge: one, turn at the corner, two, turn — until you arrive back home.

widget.prompt: Measure the rectangle's short side. Start at zero and cover it with 3 equal unit blocks.
widget.successFeedback: 3 equal blocks cover the rectangle's short side exactly.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Every block must be the same size, or the count means nothing.

predict.prompt: Counting a triangle's sides — when do you stop?
predict.reveal: The outline closes; arriving home means every side has been walked exactly once.

cml.actionGoal: Name shapes by sides and corners, place them with position words, and compose them edge to edge for kgb count sides.
invariants: A shape's name lives in its sides and corners — not its size, pose, or color; position words compare a thing to a landmark; and shapes joined edge to edge compose a larger whole — the anchors for kgb count sides.
misconceptions: Renaming a turned or resized shape, using position words without a landmark, or treating shapes as unjoinable.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the shape were turned upside down, which of its sides or corners would disappear?

widget.prompt: To count a shape's sides, what should your finger trace?

options.label: Each straight edge around it
options.feedback: Yes. Trace one straight edge, turn at the corner, and keep going around.

options.label: Only the space inside it
options.feedback: The inside is not a side. Trace the straight edges around the shape.

options.label: Only one corner dot
options.feedback: A corner is where sides meet. Trace the edges between the corners.

options.label: The color filling it
options.feedback: Color does not count the sides. Follow the straight outline.

widget.prompt: Count the sides: start at 3 and count on 4. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: That stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 7.
That goes one complete hop too far. Count exactly 4 hops from 3.

widget.missFeedback: Count 4 on from 3: you land on 7.
widget.successFeedback: 7 — each side takes one hop, and the landing is the count.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 4 counts are needed to reach 7.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count stops after 4 hops, on 7.

widget.prompt: A triangle is turned upside down. What is it now?

options.label: Still a triangle
options.feedback: Correct — turning moves a shape without changing its sides and corners, so its name survives.

options.label: A different shape
options.feedback: The sides and corners all came along for the turn; nothing that names the shape changed.

options.label: A bigger shape
options.feedback: Turning is not growing — every side keeps its length through the spin.

options.label: No shape at all
options.feedback: The shape is all still there, just posed differently on the page.

widget.prompt: Mia traces a triangle and turns at every corner. How many turns bring her home?

options.label: 3 turns
options.feedback: Yes. A triangle has 3 corners, so Mia turns 3 times before reaching her start.

options.label: 2 turns
options.feedback: After 2 turns, one corner and one side are still left to trace.

options.label: 4 turns
options.feedback: Four turns would trace a 4-corner shape. A triangle has only 3 corners.

options.label: 5 turns
options.feedback: Five turns are too many. Every triangle has exactly 3 corners.

widget.prompt: Which words describe one side of a flat shape?

options.label: One straight edge running corner to corner
options.feedback: Correct — each side is a straight stretch of the outline, ending where the next side begins.

options.label: The inside of the shape
options.feedback: The inside is the filled part; sides are the straight edges around it.

options.label: A dot on the shape
options.feedback: Dots mark corners at most; a side is the whole straight edge between them.

options.label: The shape's shadow
options.feedback: Shadows copy shapes; the side is part of the shape's own outline.
